A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 44 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original nanoGPT/Shakespeare experiments in Section 5, synthetic optimization experiments in Appendix E.1, and ResNet18/CIFAR-10 experiments in Appendix E.2.

after.justification: v4 retains the original nanoGPT/Shakespeare, synthetic optimization, and ResNet18/CIFAR-10 results, including their loss, convergence, and accuracy curves.

M1.justification: The stochastic Frank-Wolfe algorithms and specialized Lion/Muon variants are unchanged, including momentum, clipping, variance reduction, and update procedures in the main text and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use Shakespeare language modeling, synthetic optimization under Normal and Pareto noise, and CIFAR-10 image classification. No datasets, tasks, or noise scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same comparisons: Lion+ and Muon+ against Lion and Muon for nanoGPT, and Lion++/Muon++ against their respective baselines in Appendix E.

E3.justification: Model configurations, batch sizes, tuning procedures, schedules, evaluation intervals, and experimental budgets match throughout Section 5 and Appendices D–E, including the 100-iteration synthetic and 200-epoch CIFAR-10 experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 retains identical analyses across noise distributions and dimensions, including the heavy-tailed robustness comparisons in Figures 3–8. No ablations or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Seed statements and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including 100,000 synthetic runs with median and extreme quantiles. Both versions retain the discrepancy between five nanoGPT runs in Section 5 and three seeds in Figure 1's caption.

E6.justification: All experimental curves and reported findings match. Section 5 retains 2950 versus 3650 steps for Lion+/Lion and 4000 versus 4250 for Muon+/Muon to reach validation loss below 1.47; appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, KKT derivation, and proofs in Appendices B–C are unchanged. Theorem 6 has identical parameter choices and convergence bounds despite its reformatted display.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same claims about unifying Lion and Muon through stochastic Frank-Wolfe, connecting the Frank-Wolfe gap to KKT conditions, and establishing guarantees for clipping and variance-reduction variants.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Section 6 limitations are unchanged, including noiseless-rate adaptation, extension to general norms, dimension dependence, and the exclusion of Lion/Muon variants without weight decay.

D1.justification: Implementation choices, NVIDIA A100 hardware disclosure, nanoGPT access information, and hyperparameter search spaces and selected settings in Tables 2–7 are identical.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix A. References shifting between pages 10–13 are existing entries moved by pagination, not additions or removals.

P1.justification: The arXiv header changes from v3 dated 24 July 2026 to v4 dated 25 August 2026. Body wording, terminology, and section organization are unchanged after accounting for line wrapping and pagination.

P2.justification: On page 9, Theorem 6 changes from a narrow box beside Algorithm 6 to a full-width box below it. This reflows subsequent discussion and references across pages 9–13; figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The full-width Theorem 6 display reduces cramped equation wrapping beside Algorithm 6, and the opening discussion paragraph now fits together on page 9. These provide a limited readability improvement. Scientific content, empirical support, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout both PDFs.
